title: Nailing the Interview
summary_vi: Luyện nghe và nói về những mẹo chuẩn bị cho một buổi phỏng vấn xin việc.
sentences: Last month I had my first job interview in two years, and I was terrified.
My friend Minh, who works in HR in Saigon, gave me some useful advice.
First, he told me to do some research on the company before the day.
If you know what the company does, you can ask smarter questions.
Second, practise answering common questions out loud instead of just thinking about them.
On the day, I arrived ten minutes early and tried to stay calm.
When the manager asked about my weaknesses, I was honest and explained how I am working on them.
I also gave specific examples, because they make your answers more convincing.
At the end, I asked about the team and the chances to grow.
Two days later, they called to offer me the job.
I have learned that being prepared matters more than being perfect.

vocabulary.example: Before you buy a laptop, you should do some research online.
It is hard to stay calm when you are late for an exam.
Everyone has strengths and weaknesses, and that is normal.
The teacher asked us to give specific examples in our essays.
Her explanation was so convincing that I changed my mind.
Being prepared will help you feel more confident on stage.

questions.question: Who gave the writer advice about interviews?
options: Minh, a friend who works in HR
questions.explanation_vi: Bài viết nói bạn Minh làm nhân sự ở Sài Gòn đã cho lời khuyên.

questions.question: What did the writer do on the day of the interview?
options: Arrived ten minutes early and stayed calm
questions.explanation_vi: Người viết đến sớm mười phút và cố giữ bình tĩnh.

questions.question: Why did the writer give specific examples?
questions.explanation_vi: Ví dụ cụ thể khiến câu trả lời thuyết phục hơn.

questions.question: What is the main message of the passage?
options: Research is a waste of time
Being prepared matters more than being perfect
questions.explanation_vi: Câu cuối nhấn mạnh sự chuẩn bị quan trọng hơn sự hoàn hảo.

title: Screen Time Reset
summary_vi: Luyện nghe và nói về thói quen dùng mạng xã hội và cách giảm thời gian dùng điện thoại.
sentences: Hello everyone, and welcome back to the show.
Today I want to talk about how social media has changed my daily routine.
A year ago, I used to scroll through my phone for hours every night.
I kept checking likes, and I felt anxious whenever nobody replied to my posts.
Then my sister Linh challenged me to cut down on screen time for one week.
At first it was hard, because I reached for my phone out of habit.
By the third day, I had started reading books again before bed.
Now I only use social media for thirty minutes a day.
I have also turned off most notifications, which makes me feel much less distracted.
If you feel stressed online, try taking a short break and see what happens.
Thanks for listening, and see you next week.

vocabulary.example: I like to scroll through photos while I drink my coffee.
He felt anxious before the final results came out.
My doctor told me to cut down on sugar.
Too much screen time can make your eyes tired.
She locked the door out of habit, even in her own garden.
I turn off notifications when I need to study.
The noise outside kept me distracted all afternoon.

questions.question: What did the speaker used to do every night?
options: Scroll through the phone for hours
questions.explanation_vi: Người nói từng lướt điện thoại hàng giờ mỗi tối.

questions.question: Who challenged the speaker to reduce screen time?
questions.explanation_vi: Chị/em gái Linh đã thử thách người nói.

questions.question: What happened by the third day?
options: The speaker bought a new phone
The speaker began reading books before bed
questions.explanation_vi: Đến ngày thứ ba, người nói đã đọc sách lại trước khi ngủ.

questions.question: What can we infer about the speaker now?
options: They feel less distracted and calmer
questions.explanation_vi: Tắt thông báo giúp người nói ít bị xao nhãng hơn.

title: Tom's Cheap Adventure
summary_vi: Luyện nghe và đọc câu chuyện về chuyến du lịch Việt Nam tiết kiệm của một người bạn.
sentences: Last summer, my friend Tom from Canada travelled around Vietnam on a tight budget.
He had saved up for six months, but he still had to be careful with money.
Instead of expensive hotels, he stayed in cheap hostels where he met other travellers.
In Hanoi, he joined a free walking tour and gave the guide a small tip.
He also learned that local buses are much cheaper than taxis.
When he got hungry, he ate where the locals ate, so every meal cost only a few dollars.
Tom booked his flights well in advance, which saved him a lot of money.
Of course, not everything went smoothly, because his bus broke down near Hue.
He waited for three hours, but he made friends with a family who shared their snacks.
By the end of the trip, he had spent less than he expected.
He says that travelling cheaply makes you more creative and more open to surprises.

vocabulary.example: Many students live on a tight budget in big cities.
She saved up enough money to buy a new bike.
A walking tour is a great way to see the old streets.
You should reserve a table in advance on weekends.
Our car broke down on the highway last night.
On the first day of school, he made friends with his neighbour.
Good managers are open to new ideas.

questions.question: How did Tom pay for his trip?
options: He had saved money for six months
questions.explanation_vi: Tom đã để dành tiền suốt sáu tháng.

questions.question: Why were his meals so cheap?
options: He ate where local people ate
questions.explanation_vi: Anh ăn ở những quán người địa phương hay ăn.

questions.question: What went wrong near Hue?
questions.explanation_vi: Xe buýt của anh bị hỏng gần Huế.

questions.question: What does Tom think about cheap travel?
options: It is only for the young
It makes people more creative and open
questions.explanation_vi: Tom cho rằng đi tiết kiệm khiến ta sáng tạo và cởi mở hơn.

title: Finding Your Rhythm
summary_vi: Luyện nghe và nói về cách làm quen với cuộc sống ở một thành phố lớn.
sentences: Moving to a big city can be exciting, but it takes time to get used to it.
When I first moved to Saigon, the traffic and the noise nearly drove me crazy.
My cousin Minh, who has lived here for ten years, gave me some advice.
He said I should find a quiet café or park where I can relax after work.
He also told me to learn the bus routes instead of relying on taxis.
Living in a city is expensive, so it helps to keep track of what you spend.
On the other hand, there are always things to do, from concerts to street markets.
If you feel lonely, join a club or a class to meet new people.
After six months, I have finally found my own rhythm.
I still miss my hometown, but I no longer want to leave.

vocabulary.example: It took me a week to get used to the cold weather.
The loud music next door drove me crazy last night.
He is relying on his parents to pay for university.
I use an app to keep track of my homework.
The flat is small. On the other hand, it is very cheap.
After the holiday, it was hard to get back into a work rhythm.

questions.question: What bothered the writer most at first in Saigon?
questions.explanation_vi: Giao thông và tiếng ồn suýt làm người viết phát điên.

questions.question: What advice did Minh give about transport?
questions.explanation_vi: Minh khuyên nên học các tuyến xe buýt thay vì dựa vào taxi.

questions.question: What should you do if you feel lonely?
options: Join a club or a class
questions.explanation_vi: Bài khuyên tham gia câu lạc bộ hoặc lớp học để gặp người mới.

questions.question: How does the writer feel after six months?
options: More settled, though still missing home
questions.explanation_vi: Người viết đã quen nhịp sống nhưng vẫn nhớ quê.

title: Little by Little
summary_vi: Luyện nghe và đọc về thói quen học ngoại ngữ mỗi ngày của một cô gái tên Linh.
sentences: Linh has been learning English for three years, and her progress has surprised everyone.
She says the secret is to practise a little every day rather than a lot once a week.
Every morning, she listens to a short podcast while she walks to work.
Whenever she hears a new word, she writes it down and looks it up later.
She is not afraid of making mistakes, because she knows they help her learn.
Last year, she joined an online group where members chat with native speakers.
At first she felt shy, but her confidence has grown quickly.
If you want to speak fluently, you have to use the language in real situations.
Linh also watches films without subtitles to train her ears.
She believes that anyone can improve if they stay patient and keep going.

vocabulary.example: I prefer tea rather than coffee in the evening.
My brother always writes it down when he gets a good idea.
If she does not know a word, she looks it up in a dictionary.
Native speakers often talk very fast.
Practice gives you confidence before a big presentation.
After living abroad, he spoke Japanese fluently.
The hill is steep, but we have to keep going.

questions.question: What is Linh's secret to improving?
questions.explanation_vi: Linh luyện một chút mỗi ngày thay vì nhiều lần một tuần.

questions.question: What does she do when she hears a new word?
options: She writes it down and looks it up later
questions.explanation_vi: Cô ghi từ mới lại rồi tra sau.

questions.question: How did she feel when she joined the online group?
questions.explanation_vi: Ban đầu cô cảm thấy ngại ngùng.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Patience and daily practice lead to progress
questions.explanation_vi: Sự kiên nhẫn và luyện tập hằng ngày giúp tiến bộ.

title: Small Changes, Big Impact
summary_vi: Luyện nghe và đọc về cách một người giảm dùng đồ nhựa trong cuộc sống hằng ngày.
sentences: Sara lives in Melbourne, and last January she decided to cut down on plastic.
She started by counting how many plastic bags she threw away each week.
The number shocked her, so she bought a cloth bag and a reusable water bottle.
Now she refuses plastic straws and brings her own container when she buys takeaway.
At the market, she picks fruit and vegetables that are not wrapped in packaging.
It was not always easy, because many products come in plastic by default.
However, she has found shops that let customers refill bottles with soap and shampoo.
Her friends laughed at first, but several of them have now copied her habits.
Sara knows that one person cannot solve the problem alone.
Still, she believes small changes add up if enough people join in.

vocabulary.example: We are trying to cut down on energy use at home.
He threw away his old shoes after the trip.
A reusable cup is better for the environment.
The packaging was bigger than the gift itself.
The phone sets the language to English by default.
You can refill your bottle at the water station.
Small savings add up over a year.
Everyone is welcome to join in the game.

questions.question: How did Sara begin her plastic-free journey?
options: She counted the plastic bags she threw away
questions.explanation_vi: Cô bắt đầu bằng việc đếm số túi nhựa vứt đi mỗi tuần.

questions.question: Why was it difficult for Sara?
options: She could not afford a bag
Plastic is the default packaging for many products
Her friends stopped talking to her
questions.explanation_vi: Nhiều sản phẩm mặc định được đựng trong nhựa.

questions.question: What happened to Sara's friends?
options: Several of them copied her habits
questions.explanation_vi: Một số bạn đã bắt chước thói quen của cô.

questions.question: What does Sara believe?
options: Small changes matter when many people join in
questions.explanation_vi: Cô tin những thay đổi nhỏ cộng dồn khi nhiều người cùng làm.

title: Streetside Flavours
summary_vi: Luyện nghe và nói về văn hóa ăn vặt vỉa hè đặc sắc ở Hà Nội và Huế.
sentences: If you visit Vietnam, you should not miss the street food.
In Hanoi, many people start the day with a hot bowl of pho from a small stall.
In Hue, my grandmother's favourite snack is banh beo, which is served in tiny dishes.
What makes street food special is that every vendor has a recipe passed down in the family.
Prices are low, so students and office workers eat there almost every day.
You usually sit on a plastic stool at the side of the road.
At first, some tourists worry about hygiene, but a busy stall is normally a good sign.
Locals say that if there is a long queue, the food must be fresh and tasty.
Many foreigners who have tried it say that they miss the flavours after going home.
Street food is more than a cheap meal, because it brings neighbours together.

vocabulary.example: Street food is cheap and delicious in many Asian cities.
She runs a fruit stall near the station.
The vendor sells hot corn every evening.
This song was passed down from my great-grandmother.
Good hygiene starts with washing your hands.
There was a long queue outside the cinema.
Her smile was a good sign after the meeting.

questions.question: How is banh beo served in Hue?
questions.explanation_vi: Bánh bèo được dọn trong những đĩa nhỏ xíu.

questions.question: Why is street food special according to the passage?
options: Every vendor has a family recipe passed down
questions.explanation_vi: Mỗi người bán có công thức gia truyền.

questions.question: What does a long queue usually mean?
options: The food is fresh and tasty
questions.explanation_vi: Hàng dài thường báo hiệu đồ ăn tươi ngon.

questions.question: What is the final message of the passage?
options: Street food also brings people together
questions.explanation_vi: Đồ ăn vỉa hè không chỉ rẻ mà còn gắn kết hàng xóm.

title: The Home Office Balance
summary_vi: Luyện nghe và đọc về ưu nhược điểm của việc làm việc tại nhà và cách giữ cân bằng.
sentences: Since the pandemic, millions of people have started working from home.
My colleague Emma in London has done it for three years now.
She loves skipping the long commute, which gives her an extra hour every morning.
However, she admits that it is hard to separate work from private life.
When her laptop is always on the kitchen table, she tends to answer emails late at night.
To fix this, she created a small workspace in the spare room and set fixed hours.
She also makes a point of going for a walk at lunchtime.
Emma sometimes feels lonely, so she meets her team at a café once a week.
If you work from home, communication becomes even more important.
Short video calls can prevent misunderstandings and help everyone feel connected.
In her opinion, the best solution is a mix of home and office days.

vocabulary.example: Working from home saves me time and money.
My daily commute takes about forty minutes by train.
It is wise to separate your savings from your daily money.
My brother tends to forget his keys.
The shop keeps fixed hours from nine to six.
She makes a point of calling her parents every Sunday.
Group chats help us feel connected when we live far apart.

questions.question: What does Emma like most about working from home?
questions.explanation_vi: Cô thích không phải đi làm xa và có thêm một giờ mỗi sáng.

questions.question: What problem does she admit having?
options: It is hard to separate work from private life
questions.explanation_vi: Cô khó tách biệt công việc và đời sống riêng.

questions.question: How does Emma deal with feeling lonely?
options: She meets her team at a café weekly
questions.explanation_vi: Cô gặp đồng nghiệp ở quán cà phê mỗi tuần một lần.

questions.question: What does Emma think is the best solution?
options: A mix of home and office days
questions.explanation_vi: Theo cô, kết hợp ngày ở nhà và ngày ở văn phòng là tốt nhất.
